content.text: {"predictors": [{"name": "Inventory Growth Divergence", "construction": "Compute year-over-year growth in inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in cost of goods sold (item COGS), using annual data with a 6-month reporting lag. Rank stocks cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "Inventory building that outpaces sales growth signals demand overestimation by management and future markdowns, leading to lower subsequent earnings and returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (inventories growing slower than COGS)"}, {"name": "Accrued Interest Burden Ratio", "construction": "Interest expense (Compustat item XINT) scaled by total debt (item DLTT + DLC) at fiscal year end, then take the change in this implied cost-of-debt from year t-1 to year t, with a 6-month lag. Rank cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "A rising effective borrowing cost reflects deteriorating creditworthiness perceived by lenders before it is fully priced by equity holders, predicting lower future returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the change in implied cost of debt"}, {"name": "Selling Intensity Ramp", "construction": "SG&A expense (Compustat item XSGA) divided by sales (item SALE); compute the two-year change in this ratio with a 6-month lag. Rank cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "Firms sharply increasing selling/administrative spending relative to revenue often mask declining organic demand, foreshadowing margin compression and weak returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the two-year change in SG&A/sales"}, {"name": "Dividend Coverage Stability", "construction": "Compute the ratio of operating cash flow (Compustat item OANCF, or income before extraordinary items + depreciation if unavailable) to common dividends paid (item DVC), averaged over the trailing three fiscal years, restricted to dividend payers. Rank cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "Firms whose cash flows comfortably and consistently cover dividends are financially resilient and less prone to dividend cuts that trigger price declines.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the coverage ratio"}, {"name": "Volume-Weighted Price Reversal", "construction": "For each stock, regress daily returns on daily share turnover (volume/shares outstanding) over the prior 60 trading days using CRSP data; take the estimated slope coefficient. Rank cross-sectionally monthly.", "rationale": "A strongly negative return-volume slope indicates transient liquidity-driven price pressure that mean-reverts, so these stocks earn higher subsequent returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low (most negative) values of the slope"}, {"name": "Earnings Announcement Volatility Premium", "construction": "Using CRSP daily data, compute the ratio of the average absolute return in the 3-day window around the last four quarterly earnings announcements to the average absolute daily return in non-announcement periods over the same year. Rank cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "Stocks with disproportionately large announcement-period moves carry elevated information-event risk that investors demand compensation to bear.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the ratio"}, {"name": "Capital Intensity Shift", "construction": "Gross property, plant & equipment (Compustat item PPEGT) scaled by total assets (item AT); compute the year-over-year change with a 6-month lag. Rank cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "Rapid increases in fixed-asset intensity reflect aggressive expansion that historically precedes overcapacity and disappointing returns on capital.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the change in capital intensity"}, {"name": "Tax-Book Income Gap", "construction": "Estimate taxable income as current tax expense (Compustat item TXT - deferred taxes TXDI) divided by the statutory rate (35%), then compute the difference between pretax book income (item PI) and this estimated taxable income, scaled by total assets. Rank cross-sectionally with a 6-month lag.", "rationale": "A large excess of book income over taxable income signals aggressive accounting or low-quality earnings that reverse and depress future returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the book-minus-taxable income gap"}, {"name": "Order-Flow Persistence Signature", "construction": "Compute the first-order autocorrelation of daily signed volume (return sign times volume) over the prior 120 trading days using CRSP data. Rank cross-sectionally monthly.", "rationale": "High persistence in signed order flow indicates ongoing informed accumulation, and such stocks continue to drift in the direction of that flow.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of signed-volume autocorrelation combined with positive recent flow"}, {"name": "Receivables Quality Deterioration", "construction": "Compute accounts receivable (Compustat item RECT) divided by sales (item SALE), and take the two-year change with a 6-month lag. Rank cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "Receivables growing faster than sales suggest channel-stuffing or loosening credit terms that overstate current revenue and forecast negative earnings surprises.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the two-year change in receivables/sales"}]}
